Our approach

Evidence with a purpose.

Understanding exploitation is a starting point. Our work connects investigation and research with support, awareness and informed action.

Investigate

Map criminal actors and operations behind trafficking, modern slavery and forced criminality.

Understand

Produce independent research that makes complex issues clearer for the public and practitioners.

Support

Work directly and through networks to connect affected people with relevant assistance.

Prevent

Contribute evidence to efforts that prevent abuse and strengthen accountability.

Understanding the issue

Behind an online scam,
another person may be trapped.

Online fraud can cause harm on both sides of the screen. People targeted by scams lose money and security. Others are deceived, trafficked and forced to carry them out.

What does “forced criminality” mean?

It describes situations where people are compelled to commit criminal acts. In the online scam industry, this can involve recruitment through false job offers, confiscated documents, confinement, threats and violence.

01 / THE PEOPLE TARGETED

Financial loss. Lasting harm.

Scams reach people across borders, affecting savings, relationships and wellbeing. Their impact extends beyond the transaction itself.

02 / THE PEOPLE COERCED

Deceived into exploitation.

Some people inside scam operations were promised legitimate employment, then trapped and coerced into defrauding others.

03 / THE SYSTEMS BEHIND IT

Networks that need scrutiny.

Research and investigation help explain how these operations function, who benefits, and where responses need to improve.

Research & publications

Evidence worth exploring.

Books and research featured by EOS Collective, opening up the realities of forced criminality and exploitation.

3 featured publications

Co-published volume

Scammed: Dissecting Cyber Slavery in Southeast Asia

Co-published by EOS Collective, with contributions from EOS members.

An examination of trafficking and coercion within Southeast Asia’s online scam industry, and the harm reaching beyond it.

Book

Scam: Inside Southeast Asia’s Cybercrime Compounds

Ivan Franceschini, Ling Li and Mark Bo

Research and reporting on the operations, interests and human experiences within the region’s cybercrime compounds.

Research article

A New Type of Victim?

Ivan Franceschini, Ling Li, Yige Hu and Mark Bo

About the collective

Different perspectives.
A shared purpose.

Formed in 2024, EOS Collective brings together people whose paths crossed through work on exploitation and forced criminality.

EOS Collective APS is a nonprofit association based in Italy. Its work combines research, investigation and public awareness, alongside support through its networks.

The collective brings together experience from different fields to better understand the systems behind exploitation and the experiences of those affected.

  • Research
  • Journalism
  • Academia
  • Survivor support
